summary: This roadmap develops the analytic geometry and cohomology of non-proper p-adic curves, from Stein exhaustions and coherent duality to the period diagram for a curve and its computation on the Drinfeld tower. It also provides finite-coefficient finiteness, non-admissibility over larger local fields, and the comparison between arithmetic and geometric completions. Its all-dimensional Stein layers are reusable independently of tower geometry.

nodes.title: Quasi-Stein and Stein exhaustions
nodes.statement: A separated analytic space X locally of finite type over a complete nonarchimedean field K is quasi-Stein if it has a countable increasing admissible affinoid cover U_i with dense restriction O(U_{i+1})→O(U_i). A relatively compact Stein exhaustion additionally has U_i relatively compact in U_{i+1}. The exhaustion is auxiliary data; the property is existential. Finite-dimensional means a uniform bound on local dimensions. Use the stronger exhaustion for differential closedness and compact-support limits.
hypotheses: K complete and nontrivially valued; X separated and locally of finite type.
proofSteps: Use the affinoid subspace and restriction notions of AdicSpacesPartII:R0.
Form the two exhaustion structures with their cofinal refinements; prove independence of the chosen cofinal sequence.
acceptance: A closed affinoid is quasi-Stein by its constant exhaustion, without acquiring the stronger relative-compactness property automatically.

The closedness proof uses the relatively compact exhaustion.

nodes.title: Coherent Fréchet limits and Kiehl A/B
nodes.statement: For a quasi-Stein X and coherent F, F(X)=lim_i F(U_i) with its canonical complete Hausdorff Fréchet topology; the restriction maps F(X)→F(U_i) have dense image. The countable system has R¹lim F(U_i)=0, H^q(X,F)=0 for q>0, and global sections generate every stalk. Exact sequences of coherent sheaves give strict exact sequences of global Fréchet spaces. These assertions are invariant under cofinal exhaustion.
hypotheses: X as S0/exhaustion; each F(U_i) has its finite-affinoid-module Banach topology.
proofSteps: Apply affinoid coherent equivalence and Tate acyclicity to the cover and its finite intersections.
Use the dense-transition Mittag–Leffler approximation argument to solve the difference map on the product and prove R¹lim=0.
Apply the exhaustion spectral sequence for B, and approximate local generators with successive correction for A; use the Fréchet open-mapping theorem for strictness.
acceptance: For an open disc and F=O, the limit is the convergent-on-each-smaller-disc function space, not the Tate algebra of the closed unit disc.
Strictness is obtained from a surjection of Fréchet spaces, rather than from algebraic exactness alone.

nodes.title: Analytic Serre–Swan with uniform bounds
nodes.statement: If X is quasi-Stein with uniformly bounded local dimension, global sections give an equivalence between vector bundles whose ranks are uniformly bounded and finitely generated projective O(X)-modules. The inverse is sheafification of a direct summand of a finite free module. The equivalence respects tensor products, duals and pullbacks for which the stated hypotheses hold. The canonical topology on a finite projective module is its direct-summand Fréchet topology.
hypotheses: Uniform bounds on dimension and bundle rank; X quasi-Stein.
proofSteps: Use Kiehl A/B and the finite-generation theorem under the two uniform bounds, as in Kohlhaase Theorem A.2.
Split a finite free sheaf presentation using the vanishing of the appropriate coherent H¹.
Identify the two unit/counit maps on affinoids and compare the direct-summand and inverse-limit topologies.
acceptance: A disjoint union with unbounded ranks is excluded; a finite free rank-r bundle gives O(X)^r with the product topology.

sources.match: Gives the vector-bundle/global-projective equivalence with uniform rank and dimension bounds.

nodes.title: Finite-flat functions over a quasi-Stein base
nodes.statement: For finite flat f:Y→X between quasi-Stein spaces, assume X has bounded local dimension and Y has finitely many connected components. Then O(Y) is a finite projective O(X)-module in the canonical topologies. If Y is nonempty and X is connected and normal, it is faithfully flat. In particular this applies to a finite étale tower level over the half-plane.
hypotheses: All finiteness and connectedness assumptions are retained; the stronger conclusion requires normal connected X.
proofSteps: Finite flat pushforward is locally free. Finitely many components upstairs bounds its locally constant degree.
Apply the bounded-rank analytic Serre–Swan theorem.
For faithfulness use openness and closedness of the nonempty finite-flat image and connectedness of the normal base.
acceptance: A disjoint degree-r étale cover gives a free rank-r module; an empty source cannot be faithfully flat.

sources.match: Proves the finite-projective and faithful-flatness assertions with precisely these geometric finiteness assumptions.

nodes.title: Cohomology with proper closed supports
nodes.statement: For separated X locally of finite type over Spa(K,O_K) and an analytic sheaf F, define RΓ_c(X,F) as the filtered colimit of RΓ_Z(X,F) over closed subsets Z of X proper over Spa(K,O_K). Local cohomology is the fibre of RΓ(X,F)→RΓ(X minus Z,F). For coherent sheaves retain the natural locally convex, or solid, derived realization and its comparison to the classical groups when justified. Supports are closed pseudoadic subsets; they need not be closed analytic subspaces.
hypotheses: The support family is the family of proper closed subsets, ordered by inclusion.
proofSteps: Use local-cohomology fibres and the union of two proper closed supports to form a filtered support system.
Construct transition maps and maps induced by coefficient morphisms; prove the localization triangle before taking cohomology.
Compare the derived topological realization through the functional-analysis input requested for this layer.
acceptance: On proper X this returns ordinary cohomology; on a nonproper space the support condition remains present.

nodes.title: Coherent Stein concentration and Serre duality
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p, X a smooth Stein space of pure dimension d, and E a finite locally free O_X-module. Then H_c^q(X,E)=0 for q≠d. The pairing H_c^d(X,E) × Γ(X,Hom(E,Ω_X^d))→K obtained by evaluation and trace is perfect in the continuous topological sense: the first factor is the strong continuous dual of the nuclear Fréchet second factor and is an LB space of compact type. A coefficient map E→E′ is transposed to Hom(E′,Ω^d)→Hom(E,Ω^d). The solid realization has this classical realization. The corresponding statement over C requires the separately recorded functional-analysis extension; it is not inferred from spherical completeness.
hypotheses: K finite over Q_p for the classical strong-dual proof; X smooth, pure-dimensional and with relatively compact Stein exhaustion; E finite locally free.
proofSteps: Apply affinoid residue duality on relatively compact pieces and coherent Theorem B to the dual bundle.
Pass to the support colimit and the dual projective limit using compact restriction maps and the imported nuclear/compact-type duality.
Identify the residue trace on overlaps; prove independence of the exhaustion and naturality by the evaluation pairing.
For the C-valued tower use the explicit scalar-extension/solid-duality request rather than a Hahn–Banach assertion over C.
acceptance: For d=0 and a finite set of K-points the pairing is the sum of pointwise evaluations.
For d=1, E=O gives H_c¹(O)=Ω¹(X)′; replacing Ω¹ by O gives the wrong dual.
Neither singular X nor mixed dimensions is silently included.

sources.match: Gives coherent concentration, compact-type LB topology and the continuous dual description for smooth pure-dimensional Stein spaces.

Coherent acyclicity identifies the first with the complex of global forms; support cohomology uses the total support double complex, not degreewise sections with compact support. Give cohomology the quotient topology and prove Hausdorffness only after differential strictness.
hypotheses: X smooth of bounded dimension; use continuous analytic differentials already owned by AdicSpacesPartII.
proofSteps: Import the de Rham sheaf complex, not algebraic differentials of the infinite-dimensional section ring.
Use the coherent acyclicity and support functor to make the two derived global complexes and the natural cup product.
Construct the trace pairing of total degree 2d from the coherent degree-d trace.

nodes.title: Closed differentials on a Stein space
nodes.statement: Over a complete discretely valued field K of characteristic zero, for a smooth rigid Stein space X with relatively compact affinoid exhaustion, each d:Ω^i(X)→Ω^{i+1}(X) has closed image. Consequently H_dR^i(X) is a Hausdorff Fréchet space and the de Rham complex is strict. The affinoid-dagger analogue is imported from AdicSpacesPartII:F1/dagger-strict-differentials, not replanned here; no assertion covers arbitrary smooth completed affinoids.
hypotheses: Characteristic zero and discrete valuation; the strong Stein exhaustion, or a smooth affinoid dagger space.
proofSteps: Choose relatively compact pieces whose de Rham cohomology is finite-dimensional by GK04 Theorem 3.1.
Use Mittag–Leffler on these finite-dimensional cohomology systems and coherent R¹lim vanishing on forms.
Show R¹lim of the image system vanishes, identify the global image with its inverse limit, and conclude closedness.
acceptance: The open disc has H_dR¹=0; the completed closed-disc Tate algebra is not covered by the affinoid-dagger assertion.

nodes.title: Topological de Rham duality
nodes.statement: For K finite over Q_p and X smooth Stein of pure dimension d, the cup/trace pairings identify H_dR^i(X) with the strong continuous dual of H_dR,c^{2d−i}(X), and conversely, in the strict Fréchet/compact-type categories. In particular on a Stein curve the strict exact sequence 0→H_dR,c¹(X)→H_c¹(X,O)→O(X)′→H_dR⁰(X)′→0 is the transpose of 0→H_dR⁰(X)→O(X)→Ω¹(X)→H_dR¹(X)→0. Extension to the C-valued tower categories is a named missing input, not an unproved algebraic-dual replacement.
hypotheses: X smooth and pure-dimensional; K finite over Q_p; all differentials use their proved strict topologies.
proofSteps: Dualize the global de Rham complex termwise using coherent Serre duality.
Use strictness to commute cohomology with strong duality, with the total-degree shift d from forms and d from coherent supports.
Apply reflexivity of nuclear Fréchet/compact-type duality for the reverse identification.
acceptance: For a connected open disc H_dR⁰=K pairs with H_dR,c²=K, and both middle-degree groups vanish.

nodes.title: Hodge–Tate cohomology on an affinoid or Stein curve
nodes.statement: For a smooth analytic curve X/C, ν:X_proét→X_ét gives 0→H¹_ét(X,O)→H¹_proét(X,Ô)→Ω¹(X)(−1)→H²_ét(X,O). If X is affinoid or Stein, the outside coherent groups vanish and the middle edge map is a natural topological isomorphism H¹_proét(X,Ô)=Ω¹(X)(−1). This is the geometric, not arithmetic, Hodge–Tate edge map.

nodes.title: Disc and annulus pro-étale cohomology
nodes.statement: For an open disc D/C, exp identifies O(D)/C topologically with H¹_proét(D,Q_p(1)), and dlog corresponds to d. For an open annulus A, there is a strict exact sequence 0→O(A)/C→H¹_proét(A,Q_p(1))→Q_p→0; the last map is the residue of dlog and sends the Kummer class of the coordinate to one. In both cases dlog is a closed topological embedding. The annulus has a nonzero residue term even though the disc does not.
hypotheses: Both boundaries of the annulus are open; coordinates and residue orientation are fixed.
proofSteps: Use Kummer theory, vanishing of Picard groups on the closed subdiscs/subannuli, and units modulo constants.
Construct logarithms after restricting to a strictly smaller radius, where a uniform convergence bound is available.
Pass to the pro-system limit; split off the annular integral exponent and normalize its Kummer residue.
acceptance: The class of z on an annulus has residue one; it has no analogue as a unit on the disc.
Do not extend log continuously to the p-adic completion at a fixed affinoid radius without shrinking.

nodes.title: Strict restriction and finite kernel images
nodes.statement: If U is strictly contained in a smooth affinoid curve V/C, then a sequence c_m in H¹_proét(V,Q_p(1)) with dlog(c_m)→0 can, after restriction to U, be corrected by elements of ker dlog_U to converge to zero. The image of ker dlog_V in ker dlog_U is finite-dimensional over Q_p. These are restriction statements; neither asserts that the entire kernel on an arbitrary Stein curve is finite-dimensional.
hypotheses: A strict affinoid inclusion for which the compactification by discs and annuli used in CDN20 is available.
proofSteps: Compactify a slightly enlarged affinoid to a proper smooth curve and use the disc/annulus computations on the complement and overlaps.
Apply Mayer–Vietoris and proper Hodge–Tate comparison to isolate a finite-dimensional error.
Use the controlled open-mapping lift on the resulting Banach maps, then restrict to U.
acceptance: The correction is made in ker dlog on U, and no bounded-dimensional claim is propagated to the global kernel.

The connecting map identifies ker(dlog) with ker(iota_can), as topological spaces with their specified ambient maps; the two kernels are not literally the same subsets of one ambient space.

proofSteps: Apply strict restriction along the exhaustion to obtain the required Mittag–Leffler condition on kernel images.
Correct compatible lifts and use the limit criterion to prove closedness of dlog and hence iota_can.

Construct λ with the lower period row. On strict affinoids prove injectivity by proper compactification and Mayer–Vietoris, then pass to the limit; prove its image closed by the same controlled-lift argument.

nodes.title: Fundamental diagram of a Stein curve
nodes.statement: For X/C smooth Stein with finitely many components, write C^{π₀(X)} for componentwise constants. There is a natural commutative diagram with strict exact rows 0→C^{π₀(X)}→O(X) --exp→H¹_proét(X,Q_p(1))→HKtilde(X)→0 and 0→C^{π₀(X)}→O(X) --d→Ω¹(X)→H_dR¹(X)→0. The vertical maps on the constants and function terms are identities, the middle cohomology-to-forms map is dlog, and the right map is iota_can. All maps have closed image. Its kernels have the canonical comparison of C0/closed-kernel-comparison. The map exp is the sheaf-cohomological Kummer exponential, defined locally by p^{-m} times the Kummer class of exp(p^m f), not by a globally convergent exponential series on every f.
hypotheses: X smooth Stein over C, finitely many connected components; C-valued differential closedness as explicitly recorded.
proofSteps: Take cohomology of the two imported exact period-sheaf rows and use the Hodge–Tate edge computation.
Identify the first connecting map with the local scaled Kummer exponential and show dlog(exp(f))=df.
Identify the first kernel with componentwise constants and the lower quotient with H_dR¹; apply the closed-image and kernel theorem.
acceptance: For the disc the right terms vanish; for an annulus the right map is Q_p→C via the normalized residue.
A disconnected finite union has one constant per component, rather than a single diagonal C.

nodes.statement: For smooth proper X_K over a finite extension K/Q_p and X=X_K×_K C, HKtilde(X) identifies naturally with (B_st^+⊗_{Q_p^nr}D_pst(H¹_ét(X,Q_p)))^{φ=p,N=0}, and hence with the corresponding proper Hyodo–Kato period term. All field extensions, filtration maps and the passage to plus periods use the proper potentially semistable comparison. This statement is not a nonproper Stein comparison theorem.
hypotheses: X_K proper and smooth; finite K/Q_p.
proofSteps: Use proper comparison to identify period-sheaf H¹ with periods tensored with H¹_ét.
Compare its map to H¹(Ô) with the Hodge–Tate projection.
Intersect the filtered semistable eigenspace with B_dR^+⊗H_dR¹ to recover B_st^+ and its kernel.
acceptance: For P¹ the term is zero; properness remains an explicit hypothesis.

sources.match: Identifies the original universal kernel for a proper curve by semistable comparison.

nodes.title: Mass-zero boundary distributions
nodes.statement: Let F/Q_p be finite and B=P¹(F), a compact totally disconnected space. For a commutative coefficient ring R, define the algebraic mass of μ in Hom_R(LC(B,R),R) to be μ(1), and let D₀(B,R) be its kernel. Equivalently D₀ is the inverse limit of mass-zero functions on finite clopen partitions, with transition given by summing over fibres. For R=Z or Z/p^k this is the boundary model of the smooth Steinberg dual. For p-adic coefficients distinguish continuous and locally analytic functions modulo constants: their continuous strong/weak duals are used only with the stated topology. Dirac difference δ_a−δ_b has mass zero. This constructs the boundary realization; it does not construct general parabolic induction.
hypotheses: B compact and totally disconnected; coefficient and function-space topology specified for each realization.
proofSteps: Take the kernel of evaluation on the constant one function using existing linear maps.
Identify a locally constant function with a function on a finite clopen partition; dualize the filtered union and record the inverse-limit topology.
Import the smooth-induction model from SR.2 and the locally analytic/continuous function carriers from LR.0 to identify the corresponding quotient-by-constants dual.
acceptance: The compact boundary is P¹(F), including infinity; mass means evaluation at one, not the value at a chosen point.

sources.match: Distinguishes the smooth, continuous and analytic Steinberg topologies and describes their mass-zero boundary duals.
Uses mass-zero Dirac combinations for the Cauchy transform.

nodes.title: Units and boundary exponents on a rational affinoid
nodes.statement: For connected affinoid U⊂P¹_C with complement a finite union of open balls indexed by S, every unit is a constant times a principal unit times a rational function with divisor supported at chosen points of those balls, with integer exponents summing to zero. Modulo C× and principal units this gives the kernel of the sum map Z^S→Z. The principal-unit kernel is (1+O^{++}(U))/(1+m_C). The boundary class of (z−a)/(z−b) is δ_a−δ_b, with the infinity convention supplied by a local parameter.
hypotheses: U connected rational affinoid of the indicated type; the choice of puncture representatives changes only the principal-unit part.
proofSteps: Factor the divisor of a rational approximation to the unit across complementary balls.
Divide out its rational divisor factor and normalize a constant so that the remaining unit has sup-norm distance less than one from one.
Identify uniqueness by reduction and the degree-zero divisor relation.
acceptance: A ratio of two linear factors has weights +1 and −1; a nonzero constant has zero weights.

sources.match: Computes the unit factorization and the exact boundary-weight sequence.

nodes.title: Half-plane inverse limits of units
nodes.statement: Let Ω=P¹_C minus P¹(F), exhausted by the standard tree-ball affinoids U_i. Then Pic(U_i)=0, R¹lim O(U_i)×=0, lim(1+O^{++}(U_i))=1+m_C and R¹lim(1+O^{++}(U_i))=0; consequently Pic(Ω)=0. The reduction-vanishing estimate on the smaller tree ball gives the uniform contraction needed for the principal-unit limit. This is an assertion about compatible principal units, not a claim that all analytic functions on Ω are bounded.
hypotheses: The standard semistable tree-ball exhaustion, with its finite residue boundary sets.
proofSteps: Use the rational-affinoid unit description and the semistable reduction to control each norm on the preceding exhaustion member.
Iterate the divisibility estimate to show compatible principal units are scalar and solve the unit difference-map equation.
Apply the Picard descent exact sequence along the exhaustion.
acceptance: The inverse limit of principal units is constant even though O(Ω) itself is far larger than C.

sources.match: Supplies the reduction contraction, unit-limit vanishings and Picard consequences.

nodes.title: Half-plane units as boundary measures
nodes.statement: There is a natural G-equivariant isomorphism O(Ω)×/C× ≅ D₀(P¹(F),Z)=(St_Z^sm)′, with the projective-limit topology on the right. A rational ratio with zeros and poles in P¹(F) maps to the corresponding Dirac difference. This is the multiplicative unit group modulo scalar units, not O(Ω)′ modulo C′.
hypotheses: G=GL₂(F), Ω the base change of the Drinfeld half-plane to C.
proofSteps: Take the inverse limit of the affinoid boundary exponent sequences.
Use the principal-unit inverse limit and its R¹lim vanishing to remove precisely the scalar kernel.
Check equivariance on the generating rational ratios and pass to the limit.
acceptance: The class of (z−a)/(z−b) is nontrivial for distinct boundary points; scalar multiplication of that ratio does not change the boundary measure.

sources.match: Identifies units modulo constants with the smooth integral Steinberg dual.

nodes.title: Cauchy transform and Morita duality
nodes.statement: For Ω over a finite coefficient extension L/F, the Cauchy transform sends a mass-zero continuous functional on locally analytic boundary functions to the differential ∫_{P¹(F)} dz/(z−x) dμ(x), with the standard infinity convention. It induces the natural G-equivariant topological isomorphism (St_L^an)′≅Ω¹(Ω); equivalently Ω¹(Ω)′≅St_L^an in the strong-dual setting. The untwisted vector-space identification O(Ω)′≅St_L^an requires the dz trivialization and is not the same G-action. After base change, the de Rham quotient is H_dR¹(Ω)≅(St_C^sm)′. These maps commute with boundary coefficients and dlog.
hypotheses: Specify locally F-analytic functions for general F; the DLB specialization is F=Q_p; finite coefficient field for the classical duality proof, with C base-change compatibility supplied separately.
proofSteps: Compute the Cauchy transform on finite mass-zero Dirac combinations, including the correction at infinity.
Show these combinations and the span of rational Cauchy kernels are dense in the relevant distribution and function spaces.

Use the analytic duality and the transformation of dz under fractional linear maps to establish the G-action and the topological isomorphism; compare the de Rham quotient with smooth boundary weights.
acceptance: δ_a−δ_b maps to (1/(z−a)−1/(z−b))dz; dropping the zero-mass correction breaks the transformation rule at infinity.
The closed linear span of (z−x)^{-1}, x∈F, is O(Ω): its annihilator gives μ_f=0 through the Cauchy transform, hence vanishes by Morita duality. This is the S and μ_f argument used in DLB §9.2.

sources.match: Establishes Morita duality and the dense Cauchy-kernel subspace.
Identifies differentials and de Rham cohomology by analytic and smooth Steinberg duals.

nodes.title: Étale cohomology of the half-plane
nodes.statement: For k≥1, H¹_ét(Ω,Z/p^k(1))≅(St^sm_{Z/p^k})′. Passing to the p-adic limit gives H¹_ét(Ω,Z_p(1))≅(St^cont_{Z_p})′ and H¹_ét(Ω,Q_p(1))≅(St^cont_{Q_p})′, with the continuous-dual weak topology at the Banach coefficient stage. The integral and rational transitions are those of étale cohomology; the smooth Q_p dual alone is a different, larger boundary object.
hypotheses: Ω over C; distinguish finite coefficients, p-completion and rationalization.
proofSteps: Use Kummer theory and Pic(Ω)=0; C× is p-divisible.
Identify units modulo powers through integral mass-zero boundary measures.
Take coefficient limits and identify the resulting continuous-function dual topology.
acceptance: The finite-coefficient boundary weight condition is sum zero modulo p^k, and the Z_p limit agrees with the bounded continuous dual.

sources.match: Computes the three coefficient versions by Kummer theory.

nodes.title: Pro-étale half-plane diagram
nodes.statement: For Ω/C there is a strict exact sequence 0→O(Ω)/C→H¹_proét(Ω,Q_p(1))→(St^sm_{Q_p})′→0 and the compatible de Rham row 0→O(Ω)/C --d→Ω¹(Ω)→(St^sm_C)′→0. The vertical maps are dlog and extension of boundary scalars. The étale H¹ embeds through the continuous Steinberg dual. The extra O(Ω)/C is a genuine pro-étale contribution.
hypotheses: The standard half-plane exhaustion; all maps carry the function/distribution topologies specified above.
proofSteps: Compute finite-radius Kummer cohomology, separating the boundary exponents and principal-unit part.
Use strict-radius logarithms and the unit derived-limit vanishing to pass to the inverse limit.
Match with the universal curve diagram and the Cauchy/dlog description.
acceptance: The right coefficient map is Q_p→C; replacing smooth Q_p boundary distributions by continuous ones loses pro-étale classes.

sources.match: Provides the pro-étale extension and its de Rham companion.

nodes.title: Effective central-quotient tower levels
nodes.statement: Start with the Drinfeld tower M̆_n/F̆ already constructed by ET.6a. Fix a uniformizer ϖ of F and form M_n^ϖ=M_n/ϖ^Z, retaining the commuting G=GL₂(F), D× and Weil actions and their descent datum. For F=Q_p and the p^n-level convention of DLB, the Weil descent on the p^Z quotient of the corresponding tower level is effective and defines Σ_n/Q_p, with Σ_n×Q̆_p=p^Z\M̆_n. Here M̆_n is the primitive p^n-torsion locus X_un[p^n] minus X_un[ϖ_D^{2n−1}]; the cover of Σ₀ has group O_D×/(1+p^n O_D). Do not identify this index n with the ϖ_D^n convention without converting levels.
hypotheses: Fix F, D of invariant 1/2, central quotient and left/right action conventions; the Q_p primitive-torsion formula is used only in its stated specialization.
proofSteps: Import the tower, torsion locus and Weil datum from ET.6a.
Track the integer component shift: g acts by −v_p(det g), while Frobenius descent shifts by +1 at level zero.
Show the quotient datum is effective, descend the finite étale cover and preserve the commuting actions; compare the two level-index conventions explicitly.
acceptance: Central quotient and Weil descent are part of the object; forgetting either changes the component count.

Fixes the central quotient and the level stabilizers used for the two-tower comparison.

nodes.title: Components and reduced-norm action
nodes.statement: Geometric connected components of the full height-two Drinfeld tower form the standard F×-torsor determined by determinant level structure. The D× action on components factors through reduced norm; the G and Weil actions use determinant and the fixed reciprocity convention. In particular an irreducible D× representation of dimension greater than one has zero isotypic part in componentwise constants, and in the corresponding top compact de Rham term. The same vanishing holds after the fixed central quotient.
hypotheses: Use the normalization of the imported tower actions; coefficients are large enough to realize the irreducible representations.
proofSteps: Import determinant/reduced-norm component maps from the tower geometry and compare them with the effective quotient.
An action factoring through an abelian group has only one-dimensional irreducible constituents in the smooth characteristic-zero component modules.
Apply the degree-zero and top-degree constant/trace descriptions.
acceptance: A character of D× can survive in constants; the dimension-greater-than-one assumption is essential.

nodes.title: Tree-ball Stein exhaustions of tower levels
nodes.statement: Every effective finite Drinfeld level is Stein. For the Q_p model, with τ_n the map to the Bruhat–Tits tree and B_i its ball of radius i at the standard lattice, U_i=τ_n^{-1}(B_i) is a cofinal affinoid exhaustion and is stable under G_i=1+p^i M₂(Z_p), i≥1. Restrictions of functions are dense; refinements supply the relative-compactness properties used for cohomology. For general F use the corresponding residue-tree exhaustion and converted level indices.
hypotheses: Finite étale level maps over the effective half-plane; the exhaustion remains admissible after base change.
proofSteps: Use the formal tree cover of the half-plane and its rational-affinoid exhaustion.
Pull it back through the finite étale level map and use coherent finite-module approximation for density.
Check stabilizers on the finite-radius tree and obtain strict refinements for the curve limits.
acceptance: A fixed exhaustion member is stabilized by its corresponding G_i; the assertion does not make every U_i globally G-stable.

sources.match: Gives both the Stein property and the congruence-stable tree-ball cover.
Specifies the cofinal rational refinements needed for boundary arguments.

nodes.title: Equivariant semistable models with finite component orbits
nodes.statement: After a finite extension K/F, M_{n,K}^ϖ admits a G-equivariant semistable formal model. Its special fibre has finitely many G-orbits of irreducible components; each component is proper and fixed pointwise by an open subgroup of G. The model is obtained by lifting the half-plane triangulation, refining to a semistable triangulation and choosing the canonical/minimal stable quotient data so the action preserves it. The finite-orbit and pointwise-open-stabilizer assertions are retained separately from mere existence of a semistable model.
hypotheses: Finite level n and the fixed central quotient; allow a finite field extension depending on n.
proofSteps: Use stable reduction on the finite collection of quotient pieces, then pull the resulting triangulation back to the tower.
Choose the equivariant refinement by the minimal/canonical triangulation argument of the appendix, instead of asserting arbitrary stable reduction is equivariant.
Read the finite vertex/edge orbit structure and continuity of the component action; enlarge K to define the model and its residue data.
acceptance: A model without finite component orbits does not satisfy the finiteness input of F0.

sources.match: Constructs the equivariant model by semistable triangulations and stable quotients.
States the finite-orbit and open pointwise-stabilizer properties required in finite-coefficient cohomology.

nodes.title: Constancy from proper special-fibre components
nodes.statement: Let a connected smooth analytic curve X over a complete discretely valued field admit a normal semistable formal model with connected reduced special fibre, proper geometrically connected irreducible components, and the stated constant residue field. A globally bounded analytic function is constant under the model’s power-bounded-section identification. Indeed its reduction is constant on every proper component, the constants agree at nodes, and successive division by the uniformizer gives a convergent scalar expansion. This criterion applies to the relevant tower model after accounting for components and scalar extension. It does not apply to the standard open-disc model.
hypotheses: Normal model; proper geometrically connected special components; connected special fibre and common constant field; power-bounded functions identify with formal sections.
proofSteps: Reduce a power-bounded section and use properness to make each component’s function constant.
Use the intersection graph to identify the constants, lift the residue constant and divide the difference by ϖ.
Iterate in the complete valuation ring; scale a bounded function into the power-bounded lattice.
acceptance: The coordinate z is a bounded nonconstant function on the open unit disc, so semistability alone cannot imply constancy.

sources.locator: Remark A.2 and proof, PDF pp.53–54
sources.match: The proof supplies a constancy argument through proper special-fibre components; the unrestricted semistable-Stein formulation needs these hypotheses.

nodes.title: Twisted equivariant tower bundles
nodes.statement: For Σ_n/Q_p and integer k, O^(k)(Σ_n) is the Fréchet space O(Σ_n) with G-action (g⋅_k f)(z)=(a−cz)^{-k}(g⋅f)(z), for g with rows (a,b),(c,d) in the source’s left-action convention. It is the section module of an equivariant line bundle; Ω¹≅O^(2)⊗det. Multiplication by z defines the continuous operator ∂; it is not the derivation. The derivation appears as −u⁺ on functions.
hypotheses: Use the effective Q_p model and its fixed pullback action; scalar coefficients are a finite extension L/Q_p.
proofSteps: Check the automorphy-factor cocycle using the fractional-linear pullback convention.
Pull the half-plane line bundle through the finite étale map, and identify differentials by the Jacobian.
Give the twist the same underlying Fréchet topology and define multiplication by z.
acceptance: The determinant factor is essential in the differential identification.

nodes.title: Locally analytic dual actions on tower functions
nodes.statement: For every n≥0 and k∈Z, the strong dual O^(k)(Σ_n)′ is a locally analytic G-representation; equivalently O^(k)(Σ_n) has a separately continuous D(G,L)-module structure extending the group action. H_dR¹(Σ_n) inherits a separately continuous distribution action. The proof includes continuity lifted through finite étale covers and differentiability on each stabilized affinoid. The higher-dimensional finite-étale Drinfeld-space analogue is retained with an explicit geometric/analytic supplier contract.
hypotheses: L finite over Q_p; the congruence-stable affinoid exhaustion; use sufficiently deep uniform groups, including at p=2.
proofSteps: Lift continuity through the finite étale affinoid cover and extend derivations uniquely. For a primitive element f, multiplication by P′(f) is injective with closed image; use its open-mapping bound to control the difference quotient, not division by a nonexistent unit.
Use the corrected Frommer completed-enveloping/distribution estimates on a sufficiently deep uniform subgroup to obtain convergent distribution action on each Banach piece.
Pass to the Fréchet limit, twist the line bundle and dualize using the locally analytic/distribution equivalence; take the closed de Rham quotient.
acceptance: Differentiability is checked after controlling P′(f), without assuming it is invertible in the chosen integral presentation.
The multi-index coefficient valuation is v_p(a_α), and logarithm bounds are norm bounds of exponential size.

sources.match: Proves analytic distribution actions from affinoid differentiability and explains the higher-dimensional extension.

nodes.title: Lie algebra formulas for functions and duals
nodes.statement: With ∂ multiplication by z and u⁺=−d/dz, the action on O^(k) is a⁺=u⁺∂+1−k, a⁻=−∂u⁺, u⁻=−∂²u⁺+k∂. On its strong dual the transpose-sign convention gives a⁺=∂u⁺+k−1, a⁻=−u⁺∂, u⁻=−k∂−u⁺∂². On Ω¹(Σ_n)′ the formulas become a⁺=∂u⁺, a⁻=−∂u⁺, u⁻=−∂²u⁺. In every realization [∂,u⁺]=1. These are operators on the correct twisted carriers, not interchangeable formulas for an abstract polynomial representation.
hypotheses: The action is locally analytic as established above; the Lie basis and left-action convention are fixed as in DLB.
proofSteps: Differentiate the fractional-linear action and automorphy factor on stabilized affinoids.
Apply the contragredient minus-transpose rule to each Lie operator and use [∂,u⁺]=1 to reorder.
Tensor by det for Ω¹, so the diagonal weight shift cancels in the displayed dual formulas.
acceptance: Apply [∂,u⁺] to 1 to obtain 1; replacing ∂ by d/dz makes the relation false.

sources.match: Computes all three realizations, including dual signs and the differential twist.

nodes.title: Smoothness of compactly supported de Rham cohomology
nodes.statement: H_dR,c¹(Σ_n) is a smooth G-representation. More generally, for a smooth Stein curve over a finite p-adic coefficient field with a locally analytic group action on the relevant strong duals and the strict topological de Rham duality, the induced action on H_dR,c¹ is smooth. Mere continuity of an action on the curve is not a substitute for local analyticity on those duals.
hypotheses: Locally analytic strong-dual action and the strict de Rham transpose sequence.
proofSteps: Identify H_dR,c¹ with the annihilator of dO inside Ω¹′.
The Lie derivative on de Rham cohomology is null-homotopic by contraction; in the tower formulas u⁺ vanishes on the annihilator and the remaining Lie generators then vanish.
A locally analytic representation with zero Lie action is smooth; use this criterion from LR.0.
acceptance: Smoothness concerns the compact-support dual; ordinary H_dR¹ is naturally the corresponding Fréchet dual and is not mislabeled a discrete smooth carrier.

sources.match: Deduces smoothness and gives its Stein-curve extension.

nodes.title: Uniformization and the noncharacter edge isomorphism
nodes.statement: For sufficiently small away-p level, write the uniformized Shimura curve as a finite union of quotients of Σ_n by the effective cocompact groups Γ_i/p^{N Z}, using the chosen central quotient of the cover. Its Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence has E₂^{a,b}=⊕_i H^a(Γ_i/p^{N Z},H_dR^b(Σ_n)) and converges to the Shimura de Rham group, compatibly with residual G/p^{N Z}, deck and away-p Hecke actions. For a D× type ρ of dimension greater than one the rows b=0,2 vanish and the degree-one edge map is the ρ-isotypic isomorphism used below. Use Γ_i/p^{N Z}, not the unquotiented Γ_i which still contains the central kernel.
hypotheses: The uniformization level and central subgroup are matched; characteristic-zero coefficients split ρ; the component action factors through reduced norm.
proofSteps: Import the geometric uniformization with its central kernel and descent datum.
Apply cohomological descent to the actual effective discrete group and use the Stein de Rham complex.
Use the component and trace descriptions to kill the ρ-parts outside degree one.
acceptance: If ρ is a character, the constants may survive and the single-row conclusion is unavailable.

sources.match: Uses the uniformization spectral sequence; the group is corrected to the effective central quotient.
Supplies the parallel quotient and noncharacter degeneration.

nodes.title: Locally analytic reciprocity under uniformization
nodes.statement: Let X(K^p) be the compact p-adic manifold of definite quaternionic automorphic points at fixed away-p level, and W a compact-type locally analytic G-representation in the stated coefficient field. The matrix-coefficient correspondence identifies the appropriate Γ-invariant vectors with continuous G-maps W→LA(X(K^p)). Dualizing and applying it to tower differentials gives Hom_G^cont(LA(X(K^p))′,Ω¹(Σ_n)^ρ)≅Ω¹(Sh_K)^ρ. The topologies are part of the assertion: continuity of matrix coefficients must be proved on bounded sets in W and the strong dual, rather than by a blanket weak-sequential/strong convergence claim.
hypotheses: Finite p-adic coefficient field; compact-type/nuclear Fréchet duality and the uniformization hypotheses.
proofSteps: Send an invariant vector to its matrix coefficient and recover it by evaluation at the identity coset.
Prove continuity of the coefficient map via the defining Banach steps and bounded-set strong-dual estimates; this is the explicit functional-analysis request when not already supplied.
Identify invariant differentials on the covering with differentials on the proper quotient and transpose.
acceptance: Evaluation and matrix coefficients are inverse on Dirac vectors and extend continuously to the strong-dual completion.

sources.match: Establishes the locally analytic reciprocity that rewrites uniformized differentials.

nodes.title: Hodge compatibility of uniformization
nodes.statement: The uniformization edge isomorphism in the noncharacter degree-one part identifies the Hodge subspace of the proper Shimura curve with the differential-form subspace on the uniformized cover and its Čech/group descent complex. In particular the identification of Ω¹ in G0/analytic-reciprocity is the degree-one Hodge map, with its coefficient and Hecke actions, not only an isomorphism of unfiltered vector spaces.
hypotheses: Use the de Rham Čech double complex and the same effective group and descent normalization.
proofSteps: Filter the de Rham descent double complex by form degree.
Compare the spectral-sequence edge maps and the degree-one differential-form inclusions.
Check functoriality for level and Hecke pullback/trace on the complexes.
acceptance: The filtration test commutes with the inclusion of global differential forms into proper H_dR¹.

sources.match: Identifies the differential-form comparison with the Hodge filtration under uniformization.

nodes.title: Supercuspidal de Rham multiplicity two
nodes.statement: Let π be an absolutely irreducible supercuspidal representation of GL₂(Q_p) with trivial central character over a sufficiently large finite L/Q_p, ρ=JL(π), and n deep enough that ρ is trivial on 1+p^n O_D. Then dim_L Hom_G^cont(π′,H_dR¹(Σ_n)^ρ)=2; equivalently the corresponding compact-support smooth multiplicity has dimension two after the dual conventions are matched. Obtain it from the existing global Shimura period multiplicity and the uniformization edge, preserving all unramified twists.
hypotheses: The DLB Q_p normalization and central character are retained; ρ has dimension greater than one.
proofSteps: Globalize π with a matching quaternionic automorphic representation and choose its away-p eigenspace.
Apply the imported Shimura Hyodo–Kato/de Rham multiplicity node and the effective-group edge isomorphism.

If globalization introduces an unramified ξ, choose the matching global prime-to-p character ψ with ψ(p)=ξ(p)^{-1} and carry its local twist through both sides; the character-existence input is explicitly requested.
Use strong multiplicity one and the two-dimensional global period factor.
acceptance: The statement includes the level bound and dimension two, not just a nonzero Hom.
The level-zero/first-cover local arguments in Remark 4.2 are alternative checks of this endpoint, not extra global inputs.

nodes.title: Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld bundle criteria
nodes.statement: On the height-zero Drinfeld period domain let N be a finite-rank G₀-equivariant vector bundle and A_m the level-m function ring. Define Λ_m(N)=(A_m⊗_{A₀}Γ(N))^{G_m}. It is a vector space over the appropriate completed cyclotomic field F̆_m, with residual semilinear G₀/G_m action. Call N a Lubin–Tate bundle if for some m the canonical A_m⊗_{F̆_m}Λ_m(N)→A_m⊗_{A₀}Γ(N) is an isomorphism. nodes.title: Dense image implies surjectivity over a Stein space
nodes.statement: Let X/K be a finite-dimensional quasi-Stein space over a finite p-adic field, A=O(X), N a finite projective A-module with its canonical Fréchet topology, and Y a Fréchet A-module with continuous multiplication by every fixed a∈A. A continuous A-linear map F:Y→N with dense image is surjective. No coadmissibility hypothesis on Y is made. The finite-dimensional assumption is a uniform bound, not only local finite-dimensionality.
hypotheses: X separated, bounded-dimensional and quasi-Stein; N finite projective; Y complete Hausdorff Fréchet with the stated module continuity.
proofSteps: Reduce projective N to a finite free ambient module by adding a complement.
For rank one choose countably many distinct closed test points meeting the components of successive zero loci on an affinoid exhaustion. Interpolate at finitely many previous points using Kiehl A/B.
Build convergent corrections in Y whose image avoids those components; completeness keeps the new section in Im(F). Uniform bounded dimension makes finitely many such sections have no common zero.

In rank one the finitely generated ideal is closed by coadmissibility. Its affinoid extension, not intersection with an affinoid ring, is the whole ring by the affinoid Nullstellensatz; exhaustion density gives the whole global ring.

For higher rank compose F with its first coordinate. The rank-one result makes this a surjection of Fréchet spaces, hence open. This openness shows the image of its closed kernel is dense in the remaining coordinates: approximate (0,b) by F(y) and correct the small first coordinate by a small lift. Induction on the rank now proves surjectivity; coordinatewise surjectivity without this correction argument would be insufficient.
acceptance: Density of a linear map of Fréchet vector spaces alone is insufficient; the module structure and finite-projective target drive the conclusion.
Interpolation uses Kiehl’s theorem, not a claimed global embedding of every Stein space in a fixed finite affine space.

nodes.title: Cohomological profiniteness and finite copresentation
nodes.statement: Let Y be the special fibre of the equivariant semistable model over a finite residue field, with increasing quasi-compact opens U_s, each stabilized by an open subgroup of G′=GL₂(F)/ϖ^Z. For an O_L-torsion étale sheaf F define SP^i(F)={H^i_ét(U_s,F)}_s in Pro(Mod_{O_L}). Call F cohomologically profinite if every SP^i is pro-isomorphic to a system of finite O_L-length modules. Call it G′-continuous if, for each s and i, some p-power kills H^i(U_s,F) and some open compact subgroup acts trivially on the entire group. Call it cpcf if both conditions hold and every H^i(Y,F)^∨ is a smooth finitely presented representation in the compact-induction sense of MP.0/finite-presentation. In the profinite case H^i(Y,F)=lim_s H^i(U_s,F), with no derived-limit contribution.

Apply the exhaustion spectral sequence and Mittag–Leffler vanishing.
Use the pointwise-open-stabilizer condition to identify the dual action as smooth; import smooth finite presentation rather than abstract group-ring presentation.

For finite-dimensional V, the fundamental diagram then embeds Π_M(V)′ into H(V)⊗_L LL(M)̂′, with H(V)=Hom_{G_F}(V,X_st^+(M)) finite-dimensional. Its continuous dual gives a dense map H(V)′⊗_L LL(M)̂→Π_M(V). Here LL(M)̂ is the universal unitary completion, supplied by LR.2; no p-adic Langlands classification is used.

Existing basic adic morphism definitions are imported, not reconstructed.

Extend the coherent/GAGA direction by the P¹ line-bundle splitting theorem with cohomology of O(m), sufficient for the equivariant subbundle argument after a large positive twist. For A0 non-vacuity also expose the algebraic finite étale deck-cover differential-occurrence input (genus at least two), through an algebraic curve owner; this input is not supplied by affinoid Kiehl alone.

Use the existing Shimura period multiplicity export. Expose the globalization twist ψ with the prescribed value at p and the associated finite coefficient extension so an unramified central twist is not discarded when comparing an original ρ.

Classical étale sheaf cohomology, Kummer and coefficient exact sequences, finite-group and covering Hochschild–Serre, Mayer–Vietoris, coherent étale/analytic comparison, and compatibility with the exhaustion pro-objects. Supply the comparison maps, not an asserted acyclicity of constant torsion sheaves from coherent acyclicity.

Import the actual log structures, log differentials, Cartier-type conditions and embedding-system descent needed to construct nonproper semistable complexes; do not replace log smoothness by a bare normal-crossing predicate.

The current endpoint is proper semistable. Extend as a nonproper successor with embedding-system Hyodo–Kato complexes on strict exhaustion pieces, refinement descent, topology and comparison to de Rham cohomology, with explicit change-of-uniformizer maps. Proper semistable comparison by itself is insufficient.

Import classical LL/JL with full Weil–Deligne monodromy, the normalization on special blocks and smooth contragredients over a sufficiently large characteristic-zero coefficient field. No new classical correspondence is planned here.

Import finite/infinite Drinfeld and Lubin–Tate levels, period maps, commuting actions and perfectoid duality. Extend its current supercuspidal ℓ-adic endpoint to the full rank-two special-plus-supercuspidal degree-labelled realization needed for the all-parameter compact de Rham dimension comparison; expose finite-level LT open-curve de Rham/ℓ-adic dimension equality and the Gross–Hopkins infinitesimal vector fields.

Import the formal half-plane tree model, small cocompact arithmetic subgroups and Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization with the central quotient and Weil descent. Expose the normalized finite-level quotient required here, including Γ_i/p^{NZ}, and compatibility with the Hodge filtration.

Extend the existing nonarchimedean tensor/strict-space foundations to proper-support solid complexes and C-valued coherent/de Rham duality. Establish precisely the coefficient base-change, strictness and strong-dual/exhaustion interchange used here; the existing spherical-completeness Hahn–Banach statement is not applicable to C_p.

Expose the continuous and locally F-analytic boundary-function/quotient topologies and the zero-Lie-implies-smooth criterion in the actual locally analytic category. Import the existing matrix-coefficient and weak-sequential results when they already give the needed bounded-set continuity; no generic weak/strong equivalence is assumed.

Universal unitary completion of a smooth representation and the identification of its continuous dual with G-bounded vectors of the smooth-dual model; functorial compatibility with finite coefficient multiplicities. This generic completion input is independent of a p-adic local Langlands classification.

Import compact-induction finite presentation, abelian coherence and the five-term criterion through their exact nodes. Add the uniform-pro-p finite-extension continuity argument of CDN23 Lemma 1.1 needed for two-out-of-three G′-continuity, with bounded torsion and an open subgroup fixing the entire fixed-index group.

Use Q_p finite-length/admissibility and smooth-dual criteria only after the geometric finite-Galois torsion invariant input has been supplied by the separate integral p-adic-Langlands direction. MP.1 alone does not prove that geometric input; its missing ownership edge is recorded as gap G10.

gaps.title: C-valued strict duality is not supplied by spherical completeness
gaps.detail: Finite p-adic coefficient-field duality has an explicit proof route. The C-valued version needs a precise coefficient/solid argument preserving closed images and strong duals; C_p is not spherically complete. The supplier request to L0 is a Part II extension, not a claim that its present theorem proves this. GK00 supports the finite-field proof; the C-valued uses are separately identifiable.

gaps.title: Nonproper equivariant semistable geometry
gaps.detail: The appendix gives the tower-specific quotient/minimal-triangulation construction. The formal geometry supplier must expose its canonical refinement and power-bounded-section identification. Proper stable reduction alone does not give an action on a nonproper model, nor constancy on the open disc.

gaps.title: Nonproper Hyodo–Kato complexes and comparison
gaps.detail: CR.6 and CP.4 presently assert proper comparison. Need the requested embedding-system/exhaustion descent with actions, uniformizer changes and Fréchet topology before constructing the nonproper tower complex. Do not infer this from a proper period tensor identity.

gaps.title: Perfectoid boundary derived limits
gaps.detail: Verify acyclicity and R¹lim control for both the generalized Stein cover and every strict complement. Acyclic affinoid perfectoid rational domains alone do not imply an arbitrary infinite union is acyclic. The boundary-support cone carries the shift −1.

gaps.title: Full compact-support dimension comparison
gaps.detail: ET.6a currently guarantees a supercuspidal realization only. The compact de Rham theorem sums special parameters too, and needs the full degree-labelled ℓ-adic realization, the finite-LT cohomology dimension comparison, and Gross–Hopkins vector-field exports. Their exact extension is requested; no equality of Euler characteristics replaces it.

gaps.title: P¹ splitting and equivariant bundle argument
gaps.detail: Current AlgebraicVectorBundles handles scheme bundles and monoidal/relative-Spec APIs, not P¹ splitting. Need that classification and O(m) cohomology, followed by the smooth-ρ tensor algebraic-Sym irreducibility argument over the correct unramified coefficient field. The general Harder–Narasimhan theory is not silently imported.

gaps.title: Positive period-space topology
gaps.detail: The Banach–Colmez node supplies basic period functors, not automatically every positive-slope tensor topology or finite-dimensional Galois Hom. Establish the precise R06.2 extension before the isotypic Banach-factor argument.

gaps.title: Finite detection and universal completion
gaps.detail: Refine CDN20 Proposition 2.12’s cocompact Čech argument to justify one finite detection window for the full edge-obstruction image, rather than just its chosen generators. Then apply the requested generic identification of bounded dual vectors with the dual universal unitary completion. These are prerequisites to the non-admissibility proof, independent of a local-Langlands classification.

gaps.title: Equivariant differentials on a proper deck cover
gaps.detail: CDN23 Remark 2.15(ii) cites Nakajima Theorem 4. Its original proof was not read in this run. Need a primary-source verification or an elementary equivariant Riemann–Roch proof: for the stated finite étale cover of a genus≥2 curve in characteristic zero, every deck irreducible occurs in H⁰(Ω¹). The algebraic curve ownership addition must be registered, through the R3/GAGA boundary, without pretending it is an existing roadmap node.

gaps.title: Separate integral local-Langlands finite-length input
gaps.detail: Need the Q_p-specific theorem that (H¹_ét(M^p_{n,C_p},O_L/p^k(1))^{G_K})^∨ has finite length and is smooth. CDN23 proves this using its separate §3–4 local-Langlands machinery. This job owns the arithmetic-completion application, not that whole correspondence. MP.1 supplies representation criteria only; register the missing owner in the separately routed integral/p-adic-Langlands extension and check it introduces no dependency back from this input to A1.

gaps.title: Higher-dimensional analytic-cover extension
gaps.detail: DLB Remark 3.4 extends the method to finite étale covers of higher-dimensional Drinfeld spaces. Need the higher-dimensional congruence-stable exhaustion, finite-étale action continuity and completed-enveloping estimates with all field/prime hypotheses; this is a supplier-contract refinement of the generalization, not an assertion proved by the one-dimensional coordinates.

gaps.title: Historical questions and excluded dualities
gaps.detail: Keep four boundaries explicit: CDN23 Question 5.18 asks density of arithmetic integral cohomology in geometric cohomology; Remark 0.6 questions profiniteness of full geometric mod-p H¹; Remark 2.15(iii) does not deduce rational Banach admissibility or non-admissibility from its torsion theorem; Remark 0.6’s missing finite-coefficient Poincaré duality cannot be replaced by prime-to-p smoothness. These are source-era boundaries, not a claim of a complete 2026 open-problem survey. Colmez–Gilles–Nizioł (2025), Theorem 1.7, now gives a derived rational TVS pro-étale duality for smooth partially proper spaces; it does not supply the naive integral Pontryagin duality used in that hypothetical shortcut.
